bypass: authorization::BYPASS: own_rows TRUE, hidden empty, own_collections 0, the reviewer_only gate skipped; every check marked `fails under bypass` was run in both modes

checks.name: migration 0024: owner_only is derived in the database from the admitted canonical schema (`claim` own, `note` shared); no writer changed
D9: a reviewer share writes record_read, record_write and record_review (plus discover and run); a contributor share writes no record_review
list: a contributor sees only their own claims and every note; a reviewer and the owner see all claims (fails under bypass)
search: a contributor's search of the own collection finds their rows only; a reviewer's finds all (fails under bypass)
target: another member's record is absent (404) to a contributor; their own and a reviewer's targets answer (fails under bypass)
the shared `notes` rows of a contributor's listing are identical with and without the rule; only the own collection differs
work_reads (the canvas page): a contributor's batch listing carries their own claims only (fails under bypass)
Ask (read-only listings): a contributor's snapshot carries their own claims only; a reviewer's carries all (fails under bypass)
query snapshot (summaries, counts): a contributor's count covers their own rows only, a reviewer's covers all (fails under bypass)
record components (records lists, summaries, ranks): a contributor's dataset holds their own rows only (fails under bypass)
detail and read_record: another member's record is 404 to a contributor, open to a reviewer (fails under bypass)
commit on another member's record: 404 with nothing written and no recovery view (right version, wrong version, dry run) (fails under bypass)
a reused key against another member's record: 404, no recovery view and no stored outcome disclosed (fails under bypass)
a contributor can still change their own record (edit), and the change is theirs (fails under bypass)
D8: a contributor's reviewer-only command on a shared row they can see (close another member's note) is refused on the dry run and the commit, nothing written (fails under bypass)
D8: a contributor's approve is refused on their own and on another member's claim; a reviewer's close of a member's note commits
D8: a reviewer's approve of a contributor's claim commits
D8: by_filer stays: a reviewer (and the owner) cannot approve their own claim
D8 presentation (as shipped): listings and the record detail show `approve` to reviewers and the owner only
events: a commit in the own collection reaches its creator and the reviewers, not another contributor (fails under bypass)
pinned answers (as shipped): an answer derived from the work's rows lists to its maker only; neither the share route nor the database lets it reach another member, so no hidden row leaks through it
D9: a member with no grant and no organization-wide share gets the uniform 404 on the work
D9: a reviewer without share_work cannot share or grant at all (member or organization, any role); neither can a contributor
D9: the owner shares with everyone as contributor: one live work_shares row with no grantee, one permission.granted whose digest recomputes from the row; the same share again writes nothing
D9: a member with no personal grant opens, lists, queries and files through the organization-wide share (contributor)
D9 x D7: through the organization-wide share a contributor sees their own claim only; the owner sees it too (fails under bypass)
D9: a member admitted after the organization-wide share is covered by it (list, open) with no new grant
D9: re-sharing with everyone as viewer revokes the contributor share and grants the viewer share in one unit (permission.revoked then permission.granted); members read but cannot write
D9: revoking the organization-wide share ends it for every covered member at once (a second revocation changes nothing); personal grants stay
D9: a share_work holder who is not a reviewer may share viewer or contributor (what they hold) but never reviewer, to a member or to everyone
recheck r1: share_work refuses the app owner and the sharer as grantee (the definer and storage alike), so no lower re-share strips the owner's rows

recheck r6: under ensure the app owner is a grantee like any other: a member's own work of the owner's app, shared with the owner through the canvas route's path, inserts the missing rows and the owner can open it; under set the owner stays refused

recheck r7: two members sharing with each other cycle on their membership rows; PostgreSQL aborts one side (40P01, or 55P03 at lock_timeout) and storage answers the retryable Busy (429), never Unavailable; the other side completes

D9 in SQL: share_work and set_work_everyone themselves refuse the reviewer role from a sharer who is no reviewer and any share from a sharer without share authority (direct definer calls under the workspace role, rolled back)
D9 x D7: with the organization-wide reviewer share live, every member sees every claim; revoked, a contributor sees their own again (fails under bypass)

review m1, m2: share_work and set_work_everyone copy only what the sharer holds personally: a sharer without record_read confers nothing; write standing held only through a live organization-wide share is never copied into a personal grant (direct definer calls and the storage API)
review n7: a share_work holder who is no reviewer can neither lower nor revoke a live organization-wide reviewer share; the owner can

review m3: two concurrent set_work_everyone calls for one work serialize on the advisory lock; the second waits, then replaces the first's role as one unit, and both answer rows (no unique violation, no 503); one live row remains

W2b review MAJOR-1: a 'none' queued behind an uncommitted viewer-to-contributor change waits on the per-work lock (taken before any read), then revokes the committed contributor share (storage answers true, no live organization-wide row) instead of answering 'nothing to revoke' over a stale read

W2b review MAJOR-1, the same ordering in share_work and revoke_work_share: an owner's revocation queued behind an uncommitted reviewer share waits on the per-work lock, then removes the three rows that share committed (Fay keeps nothing, her share record marked revoked), instead of answering 'nothing to remove' and leaving the grant live

recheck r3: the owner's revocation takes the grantee's membership row FOR UPDATE before the work lock (the fence's order) and waits behind the grantee's fenced transaction in flight; r2: its permission.revoked digest (forma:share-member-revoke:v1) recomputes from the stored grantee and removed set

review M1: the app owner revokes a member's personal share in one unit (record_read, record_review and record_write removed, the share record marked revoked, one permission.revoked whose digest recomputes); non-owners and the owner's own rows are refused; nothing held is an unchanged outcome
review M1: after the owner's revocation a later organization-wide viewer share gives the former reviewer their own rows only and no reviewer-only command (fails under bypass)

recheck r5: share_work's 'ensure' mode (every automatic or approver path) grants what is missing and never deletes: a reviewer approver keeps record_review after an automatic contributor share, nothing written, no permission.revoked; the owner as grantee reads as held; an unknown mode is refused; only 'set' (the dialog's exact role) lowers a role
recheck T1: share_work's demotion takes the grantee's membership row FOR UPDATE (the fence's order) and waits behind the grantee's fenced transaction in flight, then strips

recheck r4, r2: a demotion that inserts nothing leaves exactly one live share record (the new role, the remaining access, the removed set) and its permission.revoked digest recomputes from that stored row
review f1: re-shared as contributor, a former reviewer has no reviewer standing left: their own rows only and no reviewer-only command (fails under bypass)

recheck r2b: a later demotion marks the earlier demotion's live record revoked without rewriting its removed set and writes its own record, so every permission.revoked of a member on the work recomputes from the record whose audit_event_id is the event

review f1: share_work with a lower role deletes the rows the new role lacks in the same transaction (reviewer to contributor drops record_review, to viewer also record_write) with one permission.revoked; a sharer who could not have granted the stripped rows is refused
receipts: a receipt citing another member's own-collection row is unknown to a contributor, known to a reviewer (fails under bypass)
query release: a contributor's snapshot (their rows only) is released against the same rule; judged over every row it would be stale (fails under bypass)
D8 on one's own entry over the command path: a contributor's reviewer-only update (grade) of their own claim is refused on the dry run and the commit, nothing written (fails under bypass)

D8: a reviewer's grade of a contributor's claim commits (the same update a contributor was refused); a reviewer-only update is the owner's way to advance a row they created themselves (a declared transition would refuse its filer)
source-view sequence: a contributor's source view carries the sequence of their own rows, a reviewer's the work's latest (fails under bypass)
guest listing: a guest of a share that names the own collection still sees only the shared notes; the row rule, not the share's collection list, keeps every own row out (fails under bypass)
guest source-view sequence: a guest's source view carries no own row's sequence (fails under bypass)
review m5: owner_only is derived by a real JSON parse (genui.canonical_jsonb): non-ASCII bytes derive, an escaped spelling of own reads own, invalid UTF-8 is refused at write time
guests: a live share of a work with an own collection is refused and writes nothing (fails under bypass)

APP-191 acceptance: 25 commits to an own list in under 60 s, 26 pages open: no non-reviewer page receives a hint for another member's row, each receives its own, and the reviewer page is current within 6 s of the last commit (fails under bypass)

0024 purge exception (W3 R1): a guest account's share_events row survives deleting its live_work_shares row (the chain stays verifiable); linked_apps still refuses the delete until the linked app is removed
